procedure.method: Independent review in this fresh assigned session. Read only the explicitly pinned inputs, verified their SHA-256/byte lengths, and checked PNG IHDR dimensions against the packet and the two pinned native manifests. The packet declares no source assets and no protected layouts. Actually inspected the image outputs returned by tools.view_image with detail=original, emitted through functions.exec, in this order: R7-B03-M1 native, usage720, thumbnail320; R7-B03-M2 native, usage720, thumbnail320. All six exact views were inspected before the first transcription judgment, image score or diversity score. No OCR, crops, generated images, revisits, peer reviews, spawning or provenance-file inspection were used. The viewing order is my truthful attestation; I do not claim a runner trace ID or trace-backed tool serialization.

evidence.observation: All six entries are observed in the required forms; no additional logo, sponsor, label or invented copy is visible. See the separate first-read transcriptions and protected URL comparison.

conditions.requirement: Every role is one separate flat opaque poster at its specified ratio with all supplied copy.

evidence.location: whole poster
evidence.observation: This is a separate opaque flat poster at its assigned native ratio, with all six supplied copy entries present.

conditions.requirement: Preserve the complete title/copy; do not invent additional copy, logos, sponsors or labels.

evidence.location: all six required text regions
evidence.observation: All six entries are observed in the required forms; no additional logo, sponsor, label or invented copy is visible. See the separate first-read transcriptions and protected URL comparison.

conditions.requirement: A substantive content-grounded non-glyph visual is required; glyph-only output, 3D type alone, texture and token ornament are insufficient.

evidence.location: lower-right scene
evidence.observation: The finger, complete clip body and open padded jaws form a large nonglyph subject. Their action contributes directly to the memo-clip message and is not a token ornament or texture.

content_form.location: lower-right finger contact, silver pivot and left-facing jaw gap
content_form.observation: The index presses the short rear upper lever; the upper and lower padded jaws open to the left with a single sheet edge visible near the upper pad. The action is specific and large enough to carry the product message.

content_form.location: desk-return body approximately x=610–785, y=975–1355; compare M1 return x=85–315 and hinge x=600
content_form.observation: As the second demonstration, this depicts a different visible hinge-to-mount arrangement from M1. The functional message works in isolation, but the requested same-product pair remains unresolved, anchoring content_form at 3.

hierarchy.location: upper sheet title and two-line benefit; lower-right product
hierarchy.observation: The large title and benefit establish the product before the eye reaches the finger and open clip. The instruction is placed just above the jaw, and the material line follows beneath the hardware.

hierarchy.location: upper-left black title against white memo; lower-right clip
hierarchy.observation: Headline, benefit and the dark clip remain the two primary visual masses. The product retains enough scale to be recognized despite the large copy-bearing sheet.

typography.location: tilted memo title, benefit, descriptor, URL and instruction
typography.observation: All required glyphs, words and punctuation are visible. The benefit wraps after the comma, preserving every word. The URL remains one continuous protected entry and the lines follow the memo plane.

typography.location: sheet instruction and URL; bottom material line
typography.observation: The supporting copy remains legible; the tilted type is crisp rather than blurred into the photographed paper.

typography.location: upper headline and bottom material label
typography.observation: The title and benefit survive reduction. The bottom material label and small sheet lines lose detailed readability at this scale, so exact-copy judgments use the larger already-viewed versions.

space.location: white memo upper-left; right hand; clip lower-right; bottom material line
space.observation: The sloping paper edge creates a purposeful diagonal into the pressed lever. Text occupies the broad paper plane while the pivot, pad gap and sheet edge remain visible.
The upper text block and lower hardware form balanced masses with clear side margins. The bottom material line fits below the mounting return without touching the frame.

image_material.location: fingertip, silver pivot and black jaw pads
image_material.observation: Skin pores, nail edge, metal-ring highlights, pad texture and diffuse contact shadows provide convincing photographic material detail.

image_material.location: mounting return directly below pivot, compared with M1 long rear lower bridge
image_material.observation: The visible construction does not reconcile with the other poster: the lower body turns down close to the pivot instead of retaining M1’s long bridge back to the desk return. Attractive local surfaces do not resolve this model change; requested product fidelity is unfinished.

emotion_control.location: large white memo, gray desk and tactile fingertip
emotion_control.observation: The close, quiet desktop view communicates practical one-hand use. The printed memo links the message to the object without unrelated spectacle, and the photographic softness supports the requested product genre.

ai_slop.location: hinge support and desk-return silhouette, lower right
ai_slop.observation: The mechanism changes its visible design across the pair: M2 combines the pivot support and desk return into a compact near-vertical body, unlike M1’s spaced rear bridge. This observable identity drift leaves an unresolved construction inconsistency.

ai_slop.location: whole image, especially hand and copy-bearing sheet
ai_slop.observation: There are no added badges, brands, extra hands or arbitrary ornaments. The principal defect is the concrete product inconsistency, not the photographic medium or the use of type on the memo.

residuals: The visible compact pivot/mount body does not match M1’s long rear bridge, so this is not a resolved same-product second view.
The smallest bottom and memo copy is limited at thumbnail size but legible at native and usage sizes.

evidence.location: whole landscape composition; finger entering upper left, jaw opening right across the desk edge
evidence.observation: A broad lateral demonstration places the clip through the middle of a 3:2 frame, with a blank sheet approaching from the right and copy distributed above and below. Compared with M2, this makes the mechanism and empty jaw gap the horizontal reading path.

evidence.location: whole portrait composition; printed sheet above and clip at lower right
evidence.observation: The 2:3 frame uses a higher three-quarter view from the opposite direction, a hand entering from the right, and the printed memo as a large upper text plane. This changes viewpoint, staging, paper role and reading direction rather than only palette or crop. Product-geometry drift is a separate fidelity failure and is not credited as diversity.

residuals: Both members are distinct compositions, but the same-product requirement fails: M1 has a long lower bridge between desk return and hinge; M2 places the desk return almost directly below the hinge. Diversity does not cancel this condition.
